title: Quantization Hurts Reasoning? An Empirical Study on Quantized Reasoning Models
one_line_claim: Lossless quantization of reasoning models is possible at W8A8 and W4A16, but lower bit-widths introduce significant accuracy risks.
method_summary: Systematic empirical evaluation of weight, KV-cache, and activation quantization at varying bit-widths across open-source reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1, LLaMA, QwQ, Qwen) tested on mathematical, scientific, and programming benchmarks.

key_findings.finding: W8A8 and W4A16 quantization can achieve lossless accuracy on reasoning tasks
key_findings.quote: lossless quantization can be achieved with W8A8 or W4A16 quantization

key_findings.finding: Lower bit-widths than W4A16 introduce significant accuracy risks for reasoning tasks
key_findings.quote: lower bit-widths introduce significant accuracy risks

key_findings.finding: Model size, origin, and task difficulty are critical variables determining quantization impact
key_findings.quote: Model size, origin, and task difficulty emerged as decisive variables

relation_to_herald.shared: Both investigate quality degradation under compression (quantization vs KV-cache compression); both use empirical sweeps across multiple models and benchmarks; both measure performance on reasoning/mathematical tasks.
differs_on: HERALD focuses on predicting catastrophic failures (looping, non-termination) via token-level logit signals; this paper measures accuracy degradation on standard benchmarks without failure prediction.
HERALD uses per-token time-series features with XGBoost to predict onset H-tokens ahead; this paper provides static accuracy analysis across configurations without temporal dynamics.
HERALD targets KV-cache compression specifically; this paper evaluates weight, KV-cache, and activation quantization as a portfolio.
